test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

It was very stupid about the boy to have spent five thousand rupees on that dictionary.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**about**" after the adjective "**stupid**."
 
• When we use an adjective to describe someone's behavior or character in the construction "*It is + adjective + [preposition] + person + to-infinitive*," the preposition "**of**" is used.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**stupid of the boy**," as it attributes the quality of being stupid to the boy based on his action.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It was very **stupid of the boy** to have spent five thousand rupees on that dictionary."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "It was very" **– This is grammatically correct; "It" serves as the introductory/dummy subject.
 
• **Option 3: "have spent five thousand"** – This uses the perfect infinitive ("to have spent"), which is appropriate here to indicate an action that was completed in the past.
 
• **Option 4: "rupees on that dictionary."** – This part is correct. The verb "spend" is followed by the preposition "on" when referring to the object or service purchased.
 
• **Similar Adjectives:** Other adjectives that follow this "of" pattern include *kind, polite, wise, brave, silly, clever,* and *generous* (e.g., "It was kind **of** you to help").
